carries: PHOTOS. A run of 104 photos stopped for one prompt: the convention checker found the framing by keyword and matched 'angle' inside 'flatbread tri-ANGLE-s' — the dish's own name — then reported it as a framing with no distance. The framing is the fourth part of every prompt by construction; the checker reads it there, on word boundaries
a prompt outside the convention now sets its own recipe aside, by name, and the rest are photographed; one drifted prompt no longer stops the run
no build: tooling only

PHOTOS.command read only .env and GENERER.command only cle-api.txt, so a secret placed in one was reported missing by the other — with a message naming the wrong file. Both commands read both files, tolerate spaces around '=', and the message names the variable, not a file

the free list is fourteen meals and fourteen snacks, as publishing.json's own note asked for and no one applied: seven free meals over a fourteen-day window brought every dish back exactly seven days later, which is why last week read as a copy of this one. A test holds the count

three free recipes still have no photo (sweet-potato-and-chicken-puree, pasta-in-rose-sauce-with-chicken, baked-fish-nuggets); they are hand-rewritten to the standard and stay free. PHOTOS.command takes them, along with the other sixty

the key files were SOURCED, which executes them: a UTF-8 BOM — three invisible bytes TextEdit adds — made the first line a failing command and aborted the file, so a key sitting right there read as missing. Worse, build 195 made PHOTOS.command read cle-api.txt BEFORE .env, so a BOM there hid the key that had always worked. tools/read-keys.py parses both files as data, decoded with utf-8-sig; a value already set is never overwritten. Six shapes tested — BOM, CRLF, export, spaces, quotes, plain — and the split case that broke the run

the pre-flight counted only data/recipes.json and announced '3 images on 25 recipes' while the cycle made 56 of 149 — the imported and generated ones were invisible to it. It reads the whole corpus, and a test pins its count to the cycle's

the prompt checker read data/recipes.json and the generated ones, never the imported: ten prompts reached the image engine unread, which is the 159-against-149 gap in the log. It reads the whole corpus, and a test pins its count to the cycle's

the three week tabs, for a parent without a subscription: this week is whole and every recipe opens, ending with the offer; a past or future week shows two full days, lets a third fade into the offer, and its tab says '2 of 14' instead of a padlock — what it offers rather than what it forbids. The glimpse that sat under the current week is gone: it read as an eighth day and repeated dishes shown three centimetres above

measured before touching it: the two previewed days never repeat the current week — the 112-day rotation already separates them — so nothing filters them after the fact and the sequence stays deterministic. A test holds it

46 of 56 photos were rejected — four in five. Not bad images: the vision named the right ingredient with the commonest word it had. Coconut milk read as 'milk' on 26 of them, sunflower seed butter as 'peanut butter', chickpea flour as 'breadcrumb', quinoa as 'couscous'. The check now knows what the recipe holds: a word is cleared only when THAT word is a look-alike of THAT recipe's own ingredient — matched as a pair, never by family, so real cheese on a coconut-milk soup still fails. Seven cases proven, three of them real intruders

three rejected photos, opened one by one, settled it: the image model does not drift — it produced exactly the recipe each time — and the vision names TEXTURES. A pan-seared crust as 'breadcrumb' with certainty, rolled oats as 'walnut' with certainty, chia as 'almond' as a hedge. Confidence predicts nothing, so a hedge and a sighting are now judged alike: cleared when the recipe holds a look-alike, rejected when it does not. Never cleared: a whole nut, a shellfish, a piece of fish — no texture explains those. Twelve cases proven, five of them real intruders, and every photo published on a resemblance is logged; tools/photos-sur-sosie.js lists them and the cycle points at it

photo framing. Two photos judged good (0.202, 0.343) and two judged bad (0.495, 0.551) settled what the criterion is: not where the dish ENDS but where it STARTS. A good photo has the dish filling the frame from the top, so the hero's title only covers a bowl rim; a bad one has a small dish sitting low, and the title takes all of it. tools/cadrage.js measures it, the threshold is 0.48 in one place, and a test pins it to those four photos

eight photos start too low and are withheld in images/rejected/ — none deleted. Every framing in the image prompt now says where the dish sits, check-prompts.js refuses a framing that does not, and the cycle rejects a generated photo below the threshold the way it rejects an intruding allergen

age drives two things, and only one of them worked. A recipe's CONTENT already followed the child: the history stores two ids, never an adapted body, so every dish is rewritten on display with today's age — measured, five alerts at 9 months against none at 48. The MENU did not: the week cache was keyed on the profile's id, which an age edit leaves untouched, so the old week came back while 50 more recipes had become servable. Age and allergens are in the key now. And the whole current week is frozen, not just up to today: a parent who shopped on Sunday keeps the Wednesday they bought for, and a change lands the following Monday

the access model now matches what the subscription actually gives. A subscriber used to download all 159 bodies and search reached every one of them — the app was a browsable database. It downloads this week, last week for a subscriber, the two days each locked week previews, whatever is saved, and the top fifteen; search sees exactly those and nothing else

the ranking is per age band (6, 9, 12, 24, 48 months) and capped at fifteen: a parent of a nine-month-old sees what other parents of nine-month-olds cooked. The band is recorded with each rating; entries from before carry none and stay out

six texts promised things the product does not do: '7 new recipes every week' (they are fourteen), '523 recipes a year from now' with a growth chart that drew an accumulating library, 'Every past week, kept' when only the week before exists, 'Nothing disappears once it is unlocked' when nothing is unlocked for life, and a monthly-batch sentence left over from an older model. The chart is gone and the three benefits say what is true

the onboarding draft starts with no age at all. It defaulted to nine months, so a parent could walk past the one choice that decides every choking alert and every servable recipe; the button now says 'Choose an age' and stays inactive. The first name is typed at display size instead of 13 points, and the keyboard no longer opens by itself over three of the five age cards
